searchText: <@689161464829050960> What is step 2 there? Grandma's wallet would have a contract caller entry point that looks like the AA entry point but without PAYGAS? Yeah, it'd have an entry point for AA transactions that calls `PAYGAS` and an entry point for normal calls that uses `COMMIT_GAS`. Both could verify a BLS signature or whatever else you want. What is commit gas again? Guarantee that you will spend at least N gas within that call context Why is that necessary here? In this specific context I mean. To maintain the invariant that there's a lower bound on the cost of changing the state of an account that's an AA target Oh, right. Since you'll be calling into an AA contract, you have to commit to a certain amount of gas used so it is costly to change state for that account. Is there any way to make it so AA contracts don't have to duplicate all of their entry points like that? It is mildly annoying that every AA contract will probably have two copies of every entry point, one for self pays gas and one for sponsor pays gas. The validation code for both will be the same, and the execution code too. That could be a calling convention that solidity takes care of Where Solidity would duplicate the functions for you? Solidity wouldn't duplicate the functions, not really. It would set up the environment so that the calldata is in the same place for AA transactions and external calls before passing control to the validation function. And the code would branch on whether or not this was the first call frame in a transaction? Or would you still need two different entrypoints? Ah, like whether or not it would call `PAYGAS`? That would certainly be tricky, since you have different revert behaviour depending on what context you're in. You can always tell, by checking `tx.origin`, but it'll take some thought to make it ergonomic in solidity. IIUC, the gist here is that if Grandma wants to submit a transaction they would sign a transaction that does multiple operations in a row, where the first operation is the transaction Grandma actually wants to do and the second operation is to pay the relayer (msg.sender)? She'd sign a sub-transaction that actually does the work, and the main transaction would pay the relayer. For a simple dapp, the transaction may be `kitty.buy()`, and the wallet would turn that into a 2-part execution transaction that does `kitty.buy()` followed by `token.transfer(msg.sender, gasFeeInToken)` Yeah, something like that And what do you mean by "sub transaction"? I was imagining a single signed transaction that executes two CALLs internally. Yeah, you'd have one EIP-2938 transaction with two signed packages inside: 1) Deduct some amount of Dai from grandma, so the relayer can convert it into ETH. 2) Whatever action grandma wants her wallet to perform. The relayer would check (1), exchange the Dai, then `CALL` into grandma's wallet with (2) It's important to note that grandma's Dai has to actually be owned by the relayer What prevents the relayer from only executing (1)? Auditing the contract, I suppose. Wait, why would Grandma's DAI need to be owned by the relayer? To comply with the rules for the transaction propagation No external state. The whole idea here is to make it so Grandma's account has DAI in it, not that she has rights to someone else's DAI. Without that, all tools would show Grandma as having no DAI. And we want Grandama's account to work with tools (e.g., show token balances correctly). Tools will need to be updated, for sure. You can't really get around needing the ETH to pay for gas when you call `PAYGAS`, and you can't do the exchange until after you `PAYGAS`. Let me rephrase that. **I** can't think of a way around it at 12:30 am ;3 Someone else might be able to. But EIP-2938+ does let you transact without ETH, if the infrastructure is in place. I think what we end up with is just layer 2 meta transactions again essentially, which is unfortunate. In this case, a contract (which may or may not be AA) can receive a signed multi-call and validate the signature then execute each part of the multicall in sequence. Where the signature may be BLS or m of n multisig or whatever. Today friday at 13:30 EDT <@689161464829050960> and <@415548822983278593> will be presenting developer’s guide to account abstraction https://ethglobal.online/future/ thanks for linking <@!527027407228502037> , was just coming to remind folks hope to see people there! I hope that was a somewhat useful overview of our current thinking on AA You can find the slides at https://tinyurl.com/eth-global-aa great talk!! thanks! I also very much recommend the talk Vitalik gave a week ago, that gives a bit more context for AA in general, where we today focussed on the specifics of the EIP https://youtu.be/_DUHTJEoaX0 BTW you can add two more use cases: * Merkle tree airdrops * Withdrawals from eth2
